verdict.rationale: smolagents documents sandboxed code execution through Modal, Blaxel, E2B or Docker, plus a hardened LocalPythonExecutor. It also enforces an import allowlist via `additional_authorized_imports`, and a hands-on community report confirms disallowed imports are blocked. Fine-grained per-tool permission policies are not documented; the only tool-level restriction shown is choosing which tools to pass to the agent. missing for 10: documented fine-grained per-tool permission or policy controls (e.g. per-tool allow/deny or approval gates), in-depth sandbox isolation documentation, independent corroboration of the remote sandbox backends.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can restrict what an agent may do with fine-grained tool permissions and sandboxed execution

citations.quote: To make it secure, we support executing in sandboxed environment via Modal, Blaxel, E2B, or Docker.
we have re-built a more secure `LocalPythonExecutor` from the ground up.
You can authorize additional imports by passing the authorized modules as a list of strings in argument `additional_authorized_imports`
step 1's Python code failed because matplotlib wasn't in the allowed imports
